name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
      - 'epic/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  release-version-integrity:
    name: Release version integrity
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      github.actor == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'release/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out trusted release validation
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |-
            scripts/validate-release-pr.mts
            scripts/release-github-evidence.mts
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Validate version-only release change
        env:
          GITHUB_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_PR_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          RELEASE_PR_MODE: pre-merge
          RELEASE_PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: node scripts/validate-release-pr.mts

  verify:
    name: Verification (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      issues: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Architecture validates the exact event base/head and accepted epic history.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run policy, type, and test verification
        env:
          HVIR_REPO_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run verify

  electron-smoke:
    name: Electron smoke (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run production Electron workflow
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/production
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke

      - name: Run development renderer Performance Timeline containment
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/development-performance
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:development-performance

      - name: Prove failure and interruption isolation
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:isolation

      - name: Upload bounded Electron failure evidence
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ci-electron-smoke-failure-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  macos-electron-smoke:
    # Temporary reduced gate: terminal-presentation, terminal-lifecycle, and capacity
    # remain available through local commands while their macOS flakes are hardened.
    name: Electron correctness (macOS arm64; temporary reduced gate)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run focused unpackaged Electron scenarios
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/macos-ci
        run: npm run smoke:macos:ci

      - name: Upload bounded macOS Electron failure evidence
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ci-macos-electron-smoke-failure-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  codeql:
    name: CodeQL analysis
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      packages: read
      security-events: write

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4.37.9
        with:
          languages: javascript-typescript

      - name: Analyze
        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4.37.9

  merge-acceptance:
    name: Merge acceptance
    needs:
      - release-version-integrity
      - verify
      - electron-smoke
      - macos-electron-smoke
      - codeql
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out exact head for base ancestry proof
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Require one coherent CI attempt
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node scripts/ci-attempt-evidence.mts

      - name: Require exact candidate ancestry
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          if [[ ! "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ || ! "$HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Pull request base and head must be full commit SHAs"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" != "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
            echo "::error::Merge acceptance did not check out the exact pull request head"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA"; then
            echo "::error::The tested pull request base is not an ancestor of its head"
            exit 1
          fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Grep-level enforcement of the architectural seams (AGENTS.md "Respect the
# seams"). This is a coarse backstop that complements the precise ESLint rules
# in eslint.config.mjs — it catches a violation even if lint is skipped, and
# documents the invariants in one readable place.
#
set -uo pipefail

fail=0
SRC="src"

report() {
  # $1 = human description, $2 = matching lines (empty = ok)
  if [[ -n "$2" ]]; then
    printf '\033[31m✗ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
    printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed 's/^/    /'
    fail=1
  else
    printf '\033[32m✓ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
  fi
}

# 1. ipcRenderer only in the preload bridge.
hits=$(grep -rnw 'ipcRenderer' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/preload/' || true)
report "ipcRenderer used only in src/preload/" "$hits"

# 2. Host primitives (fs / child_process / chokidar / node-pty) only in LocalHost.
hits=$(grep -rnE "from ['\"](node:)?(fs|fs/promises|child_process)['\"]|from ['\"](chokidar|node-pty)['\"]|import\(['\"]((node:)?(fs|fs/promises|child_process)|chokidar|node-pty)['\"]\)" \
  "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/project-host/local-host.ts' || true)
report "host primitives imported only in local-host.ts" "$hits"

# 3. PTY spawning (host.spawnPty call sites) only in the supervisor.
hits=$(grep -rnE '\.spawnPty\(' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts' || true)
report "host.spawnPty() called only in pty-supervisor.ts" "$hits"

# 4. Bundled harness identities stay inside provider-owned main modules. Shared
# IPC, persistence, and renderer code treat provider ids as opaque catalog data.
hits=$(grep -rnE "['\"](plain-shell|claude-code|codex)['\"]" \
  "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/harness/' || true)
report "bundled harness ids used only in src/main/harness/" "$hits"

# 5. Raw loopback streams are transport for the main-owned pane proxy, never a
# renderer, IPC, harness, or feature-level socket API.
hits=$(grep -rnE '\.connectLoopback\(' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/web-pane/loopback-http-proxy.ts' || true)
report "host.connectLoopback() called only in the web-pane proxy" "$hits"

# 6. ipcMain is a single transport choke point. Feature registrars receive the
# narrow IpcRegistrar capability and cannot install handlers directly.
hits=$(grep -rnw 'ipcMain' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/ipc/authority-router.ts' || true)
report "ipcMain used only in the IPC authority router" "$hits"

# 7. Feature registrars cannot bypass central renderer-owner or canonical-path
# authority resolution.
hits=$(grep -rnE '\.currentOwner\(|\.realpath\(|getRegisteredWorkspaceRoot|\basHostId\b|\bdirnameHostPath\b' \
  'src/main/ipc/features' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' || true)
report "IPC features use central owner/path authority" "$hits"

# 8. ssh2 is an implementation detail of the remote ProjectHost adapter. Main
# consumers continue to depend on ProjectHost and host-qualified paths only.
hits=$(grep -rnE "from ['\"]ssh2['\"]|import\(['\"]ssh2['\"]\)" \
  "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -vE '^src/main/project-host/ssh-(client-lifecycle|host|host-options|file-access|exclusive-create|project-file-transfer|abort|transport-pool|watch-service)\.ts' || true)
report "ssh2 details stay inside the SshHost adapter" "$hits"

# 9. Host-local collaborators share SshHost's authentication lifecycle. They

**hvir** is a cross-platform Electron developer workbench for local and remote SSH projects, combining an integrated GPU/WASM terminal with AI coding agent harness orchestration, a multi-mode file and diff viewer, inline document review, Git inspection, and sandboxed web panes.

## Features

- **Local & Remote SSH Workspaces**
  - Work across multiple projects and Git worktrees from a single window.
  - Connect to remote hosts over SSH (`ssh2`) using your existing `~/.ssh/config` aliases, identity files, interactive prompts, and known-hosts trust store—without requiring a remote server agent.
- **Integrated Terminal & AI Harness Orchestration**
  - Powered by [`ghostty-web`](https://github.com/coder/ghostty-web) (Ghostty VT WebAssembly core) and `node-pty` with split terminals, terminal search, clickable file paths/links, image paste (including remote SSH image transfer), attention/idle badges, and curated iTerm2 terminal themes.
  - Built-in providers and customizable harness profiles for:
    - **Shell** and **Custom** commands
    - **Claude Code** (preassigned session IDs, exact resume & fork, context pressure telemetry, composer keybinding configuration)
    - **Codex** (rollout session discovery, exact resume & fork, context pressure telemetry, direct review send-now)
    - **GitHub Copilot CLI**, **Gemini CLI**, **Pi**, and **Cursor CLI**
  - **Sessions Overview** view to inspect and jump to active or recoverable terminal and agent sessions across workspaces.
- **File Explorer & Multi-Mode Viewer**
  - Fast directory tree, quick filename search, safe file operations (including atomic no-replace renames via `@hvir/rename-noreplace`), and Git change indicators.
  - Primary and optional side-by-side split viewer with three modes:
    - **Rendered**: Markdown/MDX (with task lists, Shiki syntax highlighting, and repository images), Mermaid diagrams, sandboxed HTML preview (`hvir-preview:`), structured JSON/YAML explorer, CSV table viewer, and images.
    - **Source**: CodeMirror 6 editor with find, go-to-line, Git blame gutter, and bounded previews for large files.
    - **Diff**: CodeMirror merge view against the working tree, `HEAD`, branch point, or historical commit revisions.
- **Inline Document Review**
  - Attach line- and range-anchored review comments on rendered or source documents and deliver review batches directly to an active terminal/agent harness.
- **Git Integration**
  - Dedicated utility-process Git worker (`git-worker`) providing working-tree change lists, commit history, an interactive commit graph, branch switching, fetch/pull (with configurable auto-fetch), and worktree pruning.
- **Embedded Web Panes**
  - Open localhost/loopback URLs detected in terminal output inside sandboxed web panes backed by a main-process loopback HTTP proxy, complete with navigation controls and diagnostics.
- **Customizable Workbench**
  - Light/dark app themes, UI and monospace typography controls, customizable keybindings, workbench health status, and redacted diagnostic report export.

## Default Keybindings

| Action | Default Shortcut (`Mod` = `Cmd` on macOS, `Ctrl` on Linux) |
| --- | --- |
| Quick open file | `Mod+P` |
| Find in file | `Mod+F` |
| Find in terminal | `Mod+Shift+F` |

| Cycle view mode (`Rendered` / `Source` / `Diff`) | `Mod+Shift+M` |
| Focus terminal | `Mod+J` |
| Toggle terminal maximize / restore | `Mod+Shift+J` |
| Focus file viewer | `Mod+1` |
| Focus file tree | `Mod+0` |

Keybindings can be customized in **Settings → Keybindings**.

## Requirements

- **Supported Platforms**:
  - **macOS** (Apple silicon `arm64`)
  - **Linux** (`x64` and `arm64`, glibc `>= 2.35`)
- **Development Prerequisites**:
  - **Node.js** `>= 24`
  - Native C/C++ build toolchain (`node-gyp`, Python, and platform compiler tools) for `node-pty` and `@hvir/rename-noreplace`
  - On headless Linux CI/environments, `xvfb-run` is needed to run Electron smoke tests

## Getting Started

```bash
# Install dependencies and build native Electron/Node addons
npm ci

# Start the application in development mode
npm run dev
```

When packaged and installed on macOS or Linux, the `hvir` CLI command opens a local directory directly in the workbench:

```bash
hvir /path/to/project
```

### Development & Build

- `npm run dev` — Run `electron-vite` in development mode with hot reload
- `npm run build` — Typecheck both Node and renderer projects and build production bundles into `out/`
- `npm run preview` — Preview the built Electron app
- `npm run build:dir` — Build an unpackaged directory target via `electron-builder`

### Packaging

- `npm run pack:mac:arm64` — Build macOS Apple silicon `.pkg` installer
- `npm run pack:linux:x64` — Build Linux `x64` `.deb` package
- `npm run pack:linux:arm64` — Build Linux `arm64` `.deb` package

### Verification & Testing

- `npm test` — Run the Vitest unit test suite (`test/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`)
- `npm run test:watch` — Run Vitest in watch mode
- `npm run test:mutation` — Run Stryker mutation tests (`stryker.config.json`)
- `npm run typecheck` — Run `tsc --noEmit` for `tsconfig.node.json` and `tsconfig.web.json`
- `npm run lint` — Run ESLint across the repository
- `npm run format` / `npm run format:check` — Format or check formatting with Prettier
- `npm run check-seams` — Verify architectural seam boundaries across `src/`
- `npm run architecture:report` / `npm run architecture:check` — Inspect or enforce module direction and hotspot policies
- `npm run smoke` — Build the smoke bundle and run Electron end-to-end smoke scenarios (use `npm run smoke:macos` on macOS)
- `npm run hooks:install` — Configure `.githooks/` (`pre-push` checks)

## Architecture Overview

hvir separates responsibilities cleanly across Electron process boundaries and enforces module seams via `eslint.config.mjs` and `scripts/check-seams.sh`:

```text
src/
├── main/        # Electron main process: window lifecycle, ProjectHost (LocalHost / SshHost),
│                # PTY supervisor, harness providers, IPC authority router, document review,
│                # loopback web-pane proxy, diagnostics, and smoke harness
├── preload/     # Context-isolated preload bridge (only place allowed to import ipcRenderer)
├── renderer/    # React 19 UI: file tree, CodeMirror/Shiki/Mermaid viewer, Git panel/graph,
│                # ghostty-web terminal deck, web panes, sessions overview, and settings
├── shared/      # Shared types, IPC contracts, HostPath utilities, keybindings, and policies
└── workers/     # Electron utility-process workers (git-worker, echo-worker)
packages/
└── rename-noreplace/  # Private Node-API binding for atomic no-replace renames
```

Key architectural invariants:

- **`ProjectHost` transport seam**: All filesystem, command execution, PTY, and file-watch operations go through `ProjectHost` (`LocalHost` or `SshHost`), keeping features agnostic to local vs. remote execution.
- **Single IPC authority**: `ipcMain` is confined to `src/main/ipc/authority-router.ts`, and `ipcRenderer` is confined to `src/preload/`.
- **Centralized PTY & SSH ownership**: PTY spawning goes exclusively through `PtySupervisor`, and `ssh2` connections are owned and pooled through `ProjectHostCatalog` and `SshHost`.

## Architecture Overview

hvir separates responsibilities cleanly across Electron process boundaries and enforces module seams via `eslint.config.mjs` and `scripts/check-seams.sh`:

```text
src/
├── main/        # Electron main process: window lifecycle, ProjectHost (LocalHost / SshHost),
│                # PTY supervisor, harness providers, IPC authority router, document review,
│                # loopback web-pane proxy, diagnostics, and smoke harness
├── preload/     # Context-isolated preload bridge (only place allowed to import ipcRenderer)
├── renderer/    # React 19 UI: file tree, CodeMirror/Shiki/Mermaid viewer, Git panel/graph,
│                # ghostty-web terminal deck, web panes, sessions overview, and settings
├── shared/      # Shared types, IPC contracts, HostPath utilities, keybindings, and policies
└── workers/     # Electron utility-process workers (git-worker, echo-worker)
packages/
└── rename-noreplace/  # Private Node-API binding for atomic no-replace renames
```

Key architectural invariants:

- **`ProjectHost` transport seam**: All filesystem, command execution, PTY, and file-watch operations go through `ProjectHost` (`LocalHost` or `SshHost`), keeping features agnostic to local vs. remote execution.
- **Single IPC authority**: `ipcMain` is confined to `src/main/ipc/authority-router.ts`, and `ipcRenderer` is confined to `src/preload/`.
- **Centralized PTY & SSH ownership**: PTY spawning goes exclusively through `PtySupervisor`, and `ssh2` connections are owned and pooled through `ProjectHostCatalog` and `SshHost`.
